post.title: Should you wait for 0% before charging?
post.caption:
Should you let your phone hit 0% before you charge it? No 🔋

Phone batteries are lithium-ion, and they don't need to run empty first: charge whenever you want. What wears them is charge cycles, and one cycle is 100% of the battery's capacity used, even if it's spread over several charges (75% today, 25% tomorrow = one cycle). So topping up wastes nothing, and phone batteries are built to keep about 80% of their capacity after hundreds of full cycles. The takeaway, on Android or iPhone: charge any time, and check battery health in your settings.
Send this to the friend who waits for 1%.
keywords: should you let your phone die before charging

sources.note: Apple, Why lithium-ion: charge your Apple lithium-ion battery whenever you want; there's no need to let it discharge 100% before recharging; one charge cycle = 100% of capacity used, not necessarily from one charge (75% one day, 25% the next)

Apple Support, iPhone battery and performance: one charge cycle when you've used an amount that represents 100% of capacity; iPhone 14 and earlier retain 80% of original capacity at 500 complete cycles under ideal conditions, iPhone 15 models at 1000; Battery Health in Settings
